rationale: The assistant went straight to the sensible first checks (coupler condition, roller ring, obstructions) with an unplug-first instruction and a casing-removal warning, then correctly identified the cracked, rounded coupler as the cause once the customer reported it and the drop history. It asked for the model before recommending a part and, lacking a confirmed part number, honestly said so rather than inventing one, describing the correct generic part type (coupler/spider/drive hub) matched to the three-pronged shape. Minor deduction only because the first message had a numbering glitch and it never explicitly asked whether the motor shaft turns with the plate removed, though the diagnosis matched the hidden truth.
